features.text: The patient has pain in the right flank that radiates to the groin.
The pain is sharp and intermittent.
The pain is worse when not drinking enough or after being active.
The patient has not experienced fever, nausea, vomiting, hematuria, or difficulty urinating.
The patient has a history of kidney stones.
The patient has had prior urological surgeries related to kidney stones.
The patient is currently taking ibuprofen for the pain.
The patient was previously told there was a stone in the right ureter, about half a centimeter in size.
The patient was previously told the stone is still in the proximal right ureter and has not changed in size or location.
The patient has not had any recent imaging studies or urinalysis related to this flank pain.
The patient does not remember the exact type or dates of prior urological surgeries.
The patient has not had any follow-up imaging or urological evaluations since the prior CT scan.
The patient has not noticed any changes in the nature of the pain or new symptoms since the prior CT scan.
